B3L01-G01-P29: 可以說是 means you could say it is. It explains or sums up what was just said, and 可說是 means the same.
It does not mean being able to speak. For that, use 可以說 without 是.
For plain facts like who someone is, use ordinary 是.
B3L01-G02-P30: 多麼 ... 啊 shows strong feeling that something is more than expected, in an exaggerated tone.
麼 can be left out, and 啊 goes at the end of the sentence.
多麼 goes before an adjective, not directly before a noun.
It can't ask about price or amount. Use 多少 for that.
B3L01-G03-P32: 再說 adds one more reason or a fuller explanation to what was just said.
Put 再說 at the start of the added sentence, never at the very end.
To ask someone to say it again, use 請再說一次, not 再說 alone.
B3L01-G04-P38: 而 links a cause to its result, mostly in writing or formal speech.
因為 comes before the reason and 而 before the result, so 因為……而…… means 因為……所以…….
Don't use 而 between two nouns. Use 和 or 跟 for nouns.
B3L01-G05-P40: Put 出 after a verb to say that the action makes something new appear.
Common verbs are 想, 做, 說, 寫 and 畫.
This is not 出 for moving out of a place, which uses 走出來.
B3L01-G06-P42: 就算 means even if. The imagined situation after it does not change the facts or the decision.
Use 也 in the second part, not 但是.
雖然 starts a real fact, but 就算 starts an imagined condition.
B3L02-G01-P51: 早就……了 says the speaker feels something happened a long time ago.
已經 only says it is done. 早就 adds the feeling of long ago.
Don't use it for something that just happened. Use 剛才 or 剛剛 instead.
B3L02-G02-P52: 順便 means you do a second thing while doing the first, without much extra trouble or time.
It is often used when asking someone to do a small extra thing.
Put 順便 right before the second verb. For a special trip, say 特地 or 專門.
B3L02-G03-P53: 一會兒……，一會兒…… says two or more situations happen one after the other or take turns.
The speaker feels the change is quick, and the tone is sometimes a little exaggerated.
Say both parts. For two actions at the same time, use 一邊……一邊…….
B3L02-G04-P54: 算了 is a spoken way to say forget it: you are unhappy but won't spend more time or effort.
It can be a whole sentence by itself, or come after a different choice, as in 我找別人跟我去算了.
To say you finished calculating, use 算好了, not 算了.
B3L02-G05-P62: 開 after a verb is the result of the action. It means things that were together come apart.
It can also mean a person or thing leaves where it was. 走不開 means you are too busy to leave.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 開 to say can or can't, as in 打不開.
B3L02-G06-P64: 經過 can be followed by a stretch of past time, as in 經過了兩個小時.
It can also be followed by a process that happened, as in 經過李老闆修理.
The sentence then gives the result. Don't put an adjective right after 經過.
B3L02-G07-P65: 用 plus a tool or method says how you do something.
Put the tool or method first, then the action.
來 can be left out and the meaning stays the same.
B3L03-G01-P78: 試 plus a verb means to try it first, before you decide to buy or use something.
The verb is usually one syllable, such as 吃, 穿, 用, 喝 or 開.
Use 試 once, as in 試躺. Don't say 試試躺.
B3L03-G02-P80: 掉 after a verb with an object means getting rid of something or a bad result, as in 吃掉.
After a verb with no object, 掉 means leaving, as in 走掉 and 跑掉.
完 means finishing. 掉 means throwing away, using up, or a bad result.
B3L03-G03-P81: 什麼(N)都 means all or any, as in 他什麼忙都幫: he helps with anything.
就是 then names the only choice or the one different case.
他什麼茶都喝，就是不喝紅茶 means he drinks any tea except black tea.
B3L03-G04-P82: 別再……了 is for telling or reminding someone else to stop doing something.
不再……了 is for your own decision, or for saying that someone no longer does something.
B3L03-G05-P88: 不僅 means the same as 不但, and it is mostly used in writing.
The second part starts with 還, 也 or 而且 to add more.
Don't use 但是 after 不僅.
B3L03-G06-P90: This pattern says a degree changes step by step, as in 一天比一天熱了.
Put 比 between the two measure words, then the adjective.
Don't drop 比: 一樣一樣 only shows things one after another, with no comparison.
B3L04-G01-P101: 好 plus an adjective plus 的 plus a noun is a strong exclamation, as in 好有趣的表演啊.
You must keep 的 between the adjective and the noun.
Use 好, not 很, to make this exclamation.
B3L04-G02-P103: V 來 V 去，還是…… says someone did an action again and again, spent time, and nothing changed.
After 還是, the speaker gives an opinion, a feeling or a decision.
想來想去 shows long thinking before the answer. 想想 is only a short thought.
B3L04-G03-P105: 終於 means finally: after a long process, a hoped-for result comes.
Put it after the subject and before the verb or adjective. Add 了 at the end to show a change.
終於 shows relief after hard effort or a long wait. 最後 only says what came last.
B3L04-G04-P113: V個不停 says the same action keeps repeating in a short time, as in 雨下個不停.
V個沒完 says the action can't or won't stop, and usually the speaker feels annoyed or impatient.
If the verb has an object, say the verb twice: 開會開個不停.
B3L04-G05-P114: 不 Vs₁ 不 Vs₂ says something is in the middle and just right, as in 不大不小.
Both words must be one syllable and opposites, such as 多少, 高矮 and 冷熱.
B3L04-G06-P115: 除了……就是…… says that if you take away the first thing, only the second is left.
以外 can be left out.
除了……也/還…… adds one more thing. 除了……就是…… leaves only one.
B3L04-G07-P117: 不是……，就是…… says it must be one of two things, with no other choice.
Don't use it when both are true at once.
除了……就是…… is different: it takes one thing away and says only the other is left.
B3L05-G01-P128: 萬一 is followed by something very unlikely to happen, usually something bad.
After the 萬一 part, 就 gives the bad result and 才 gives a way to avoid trouble.
如果 and 要是 work for any normal condition. 萬一 is only for unlikely events.
B3L05-G02-P130: 一連 says the same action or situation happens again and again without a break.
It is followed by a verb or a number with a measure word, as in 一連三天.
Put 不 or 沒 after the number phrase, right before the verb.
B3L05-G03-P132: 以為 is followed by what the speaker first believed, which was wrong.
沒想到 is followed by what really happened, which the speaker never expected.
Use 以為, not 認為 or 覺得, when the first belief turned out wrong.
B3L05-G04-P133: After comparing the choices, the speaker gives a conclusion or advice. The advice comes after 還是.
吧 at the end makes the advice softer, like a friendly suggestion, not a command.
B3L05-G05-P141: 結果 connects an event to the final situation after it.
所以 gives a logical result. 結果 gives how things finally ended, often not what was hoped.
結果 can also be a noun that means the outcome, as in 考試的結果.
B3L05-G06-P143: 甚至 is followed by the person, thing or case the speaker wants to stress.
It is often used with 不但 or 連……都/也…….
而且 adds a similar point. 甚至 adds a more extreme case. If you use 連, put it right after 甚至.
B3L05-G07-P144: 以 marks a boundary. Put a place name before it, then a direction after it.
臺中以北 means the area north of 臺中. The directions are 以東, 以西, 以南 and 以北.
B3L06-G01-P155: Agree with what someone just said, then give a different view after 可是, 但是 or 不過.
Repeat their word with 倒是 between: 想倒是想，可是我要趁暑假多打一點兒工.
倒 can be left out: 生意好是好，不過一家店一年就要用掉十萬九千根吸管.
Unlike a plain 'although … but', echoing their word first makes your 'but' sound softer.
B3L06-G02-P157: X分之Y says a part of a whole: 三分之二 is two thirds, and 百分之五 is 5%.
The whole comes first, opposite English: in 三分之二, 三 is the whole and 二 is the part.
Before a noun, add 的: 五分之四的人, 三分之二的時間.
For percent say 百分之…, never with a one before 百, and don't leave out 分.
B3L06-G03-P159: 總算 means finally, at last: something you hoped for came true after a long wait or hard work.
Put it before the verb or result, often ending with 了: 今天總算暖和一點了.
Use it only for something you wanted to happen, in relaxed, spoken Chinese.
It feels more relieved than Lesson 4's formal 'finally'. Don't mix it up with 總是 (always).
B3L06-G04-P160: 既然 means since, as in "now that this is true". It starts from a fact both people already know.
就 comes in the second part with your decision, advice or conclusion: 既然這樣，我們就先回家休息.
If the second part has a subject, put 就 after it: 我們就…, never before the subject.
如果 is for what may or may not happen. 既然 states a known fact and pairs with 就.
B3L06-G05-P167: 在……中 means in or within something you can't touch: a situation, an event, someone's mind or eyes.
Put a noun between 在 and 中: 在我心中, 在老闆的眼中, 在會議中.
It usually comes before the main thing you say: 在我心中，家人比什麼都重要.
在……裡 is everyday for physical places. 在……中 sounds more formal and is common in writing.
B3L06-G06-P169: Both mean must. Each is a double "not": 不能不去 is "cannot not go", so "have to go".
不能不: you must, because it is your duty or the sensible thing to do: 我不能不早一點回家.
不得不: you don't want to, but there is no other way: 不得不早一點退休.
Put them right before the verb. 不得不 is the stronger one.
B3L06-G07-P171: 正 + verb means just as or right when: one thing is about to start, and another happens.
Put 正 before the verb (要, 想, 打算, 準備), ending with 時: 我正要進電梯時，突然發生地震.
The second part says what happened then, often with 就 or 突然: 我正想打電話給小紀時，就接到他打來的電話.
正要 is just about to. 正在 is in the middle of doing something.
B3L07-G01-P184: 才……就…… shows surprise that so little time, amount or age led to a result: 才六天就結束了.
才剛 means only just, with 就 right after: 弟弟才剛畢業就立刻找到了一份好工作.
才 and 就 each go after the subject of their own part, before the verb.
Book 2 Lesson 7's 剛……就…… only links two close events; 才……就…… adds surprise at how soon.
B3L07-G02-P186: 話說回來 means "but then again". You add another side or return to the main point without disagreeing.
Put it at the start with a comma: 不過話說回來，網路上的資料不一定都是對的.
不過, 可是 or 但是 often comes right before it, but it can also stand alone.
It is softer than a plain 可是: it does not push back at the other person.
B3L07-G03-P187: 這麼說 means "so, going by what you just said". Use it to state what follows or check you understood.
It opens your reply, with a comma before your conclusion: 這麼說，明天可能會放颱風假喔.
Use it only to answer someone else, not to sum up your own sentence.
Lesson 6's 'since … then …' leads to a decision or advice. 這麼說 only draws the conclusion.
B3L07-G04-P189: 成 right after a verb means the action worked out: 今天終於談成了 (the deal was settled).
Say 沒 + verb + 成 when a plan fell through, or put 得/不 between: 明天的跨年活動恐怕辦不成了.
Never say 不 + verb + 成.
V 完 (Book 2 Lesson 1) only means finished. V 成 means it succeeded.
B3L07-G05-P195: 就……來說 means "as for" or "in terms of". It narrows what you say to one topic, mostly formally.
Put the topic between 就 and 來說 at the start: 就選舉文化來說，臺灣和法國很不同.
What goes inside is a topic or an area, not a person.
對……來說 (Book 2 Lesson 10) is for a person's view. 就……來說 is for the angle discussed.
B3L07-G06-P197: 得 after a verb or describing word plus a result shows how far it went: 開心得把工作的問題都忘了.
The result is often an exaggeration or whole clause: 吃得我都站不起來了, 忙得沒時間吃飯.
Don't add 'very' before the describing word, and don't put an object between the verb and 得.
The earlier 得 says how well something is done. This one gives the result.
B3L08-G01-P210: 把 A + verb + 成 B says an action turns one thing into another: 把它翻成了二十種語言.
With 看, 聽, 說, 寫 or 念 it means mistaking one thing for another: 把我看成只愛買名牌的人.
The order is 把, starting thing, verb, 成, result. 了 goes after 成: 拍成了電影.
Lesson 7's V 成 is about getting something done. Here 成 names what the thing becomes.
B3L08-G02-P211: 再……也/都…… means "no matter how". Even at the extreme, the result or decision stays the same.
Put 再 before the describing word, and 也 or 都 in the second part: 父母再忙都應該陪陪他們.
It can also come before a noun with 的: 再討厭的工作也得忍耐 (no matter how awful the job).
Use 再, not 更 or 又. Unlike 'even if', 再……也…… pushes one quality to its limit.
B3L08-G03-P213: V 慣 means you are used to doing something: 我睡慣了家裡的床 (I am used to my own bed).
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 慣 for can or can't get used to it: 穿得慣, 吃不慣.
Right after the action use 慣, not the full word: say 吃不慣, never 吃不習慣了.
B3L08-G04-P219: 況且 means besides, what is more. It adds a second reason that makes your point stronger.
Put 況且 at the start of the second reason, often with 也, 還 or 又: 可是我沒興趣，況且我還有自己的夢想.
A subject comes after 況且 and before 也, 還 or 又: 況且我還有….
It works like Lesson 1's 'besides' but sounds more formal. Always give the first reason before it.
B3L08-G05-P221: 非……不可 means you absolutely must, with no other choice. 非 means not and 不可 means cannot.
Put the whole action between 非 and 不可: 非去看醫生不可, 非立刻送洗不可.
Keep 不可 at the very end and don't leave it out.
Lesson 6's 'have no choice but' feels helpless. 非……不可 stresses how urgent or necessary it is.
B3L08-G06-P222: 畢竟 means after all. It brings up the key fact behind your advice or opinion, to remind or persuade.
Put it at the start of that fact or after its subject: 對她的要求太高了，畢竟她才三歲.
Unlike English "after all", it never goes at the end: 畢竟人不是機器.
Book 2 Lesson 10's 究竟/question-emphasis presses for an answer. 畢竟 states a fact everyone accepts.
B3L09-G01-P235: Here 過來 after a verb means coming back to a normal or better state. Nothing moves toward you.
It goes right after the verb: 半夜會突然醒過來 (suddenly wake up), 過了一會兒我才明白過來 (finally understood).
An object goes in front with 把: 把亂丟髒衣服的壞習慣改過來了 (fixed the bad habit).
過去 is the opposite, from normal to a worse state, as in 暈過去 (to faint). It is used less often.
B3L09-G02-P237: 怎麼不……，反而…… asks why someone skipped the expected action and did the opposite, often as a complaint.
Put the expected action after 怎麼不 and the surprising one after 反而: 你怎麼不跟他說，反而老是幫他整理呢.
The subject comes before 怎麼不. 呢 at the end is common but can be left out.
This one questions the person. The next page's pattern just states the surprising fact.
B3L09-G03-P238: 不但不/沒……，反而…… means "far from doing X, the opposite happened".
Put what you expected after 不但不/沒, and what happened after 反而: 他父母不但沒生氣，反而讓他去義大利遊學.
Use 沒 for something that did not happen, and 不 for something a person does not or will not do.
Book 2's 'not only … also …' adds more of the same. With 反而 the second part goes the other way.
B3L09-G04-P240: Here 才 pushes back hard at what someone just said: "no, it's the other way", often ending with 呢.
Put 才 before what you stress, and before 不: 我才不要呢, 我爸媽才不這麼想.
It can also say what is really true: 我認為李導演拍的才好呢.
It is not the 才 for "later than expected" or "only so little" that you learned in Book 2.
B3L09-G05-P247: 尤其是 means especially. It picks out one case from a wider group.
Say the general point first, then 尤其是 and the special case: 臺灣社會一直都很重視學生的學習表現，尤其是考試的成績.
Keep 是 before a noun: 尤其是英文會話課 (especially the English conversation class).
It can't start a new topic. There must be a wider group before it.
B3L09-G06-P248: Here 著 is read zháo. After a verb it means the action reaches its goal, not ongoing zhe.
With 得 or 不 it shows whether that is possible: 用得著, 看得著、摸不著.
For what actually happened, say verb + 著了, or 沒 + verb + 著.
It works like Book 2 Lesson 4's V-dào, with verbs such as 找, 用, 猜 and 買.
B3L09-G07-P250: 以 A 代替 B means using A in place of B. It is a more formal 用 A 代替 B.
The new thing goes after 以 and the old one after 代替: 讓孩子以思考代替記答案.
A and B can be things or actions: 以搭公車、騎自行車代替開車.
Don't swap the two. This 以 means using. It is not the 以 before a direction from Lesson 5.
B3L10-G01-P262: 直到……才…… means not until: something happened only at a certain time or event, feeling late.
Put the time or event after 直到 and the result after 才: 直到三十歲才找到合適的.
If the second part has a subject, 才 goes after it: 直到飛機起飛前三十分鐘，我才趕到機場.
Always pair 直到 with 才, never with 'early/easy' jiù.
B3L10-G02-P263: 只不過 means it's just that, the same as 只是. It adds a catch to what you just said.
Put it at the start of the second part: 我很喜歡這輛英國車，只不過價格太高了.
It is softer than a plain 'but'. The first part still stands; 只不過 only adds a small catch.
B3L10-G03-P265: 害 means to cause someone a bad result, like 讓 or 使 but stronger. It puts the blame on the cause.
Put cause, 害, person, then bad result: 他死也不肯去，害我擔心得不得了.
Use 害 only for bad results. For good or neutral ones, use 讓 or 使.
B3L10-G04-P272: V到底 means to keep doing something all the way to the end, with effort and determination.
Put 到底 right after the verb: 堅持到底, 幫到底, 負責到底. Say 堅持到底, not 到底堅持.
In Book 2 Lesson 10, 到底 goes before the verb in a question to mean "on earth".
B3L10-G05-P274: 一再 means again and again. It says the same thing happened, or was done, many separate times.
Put it after the subject and before the verb or phrase: 市長一再向民眾強調.
Lesson 5's 'in a row' takes a number of days or times. 一再 takes no number.
B3L10-G06-P275: 假如, 如果 and 要是 all set up a condition. The result often follows with 就.
假如 goes before the subject and is mostly used in writing.
如果 works in writing or speech. 要是 is mostly used in speech. Both can go before or after the subject.
B3L10-G07-P276: 為了……而…… links a goal with what someone does to reach it.
Put the goal after 為了 and the action after 而: 他為了挑戰臺灣最高的高山，而每天慢跑一小時.
The subject goes before 為了: 林伯伯為了健康而努力.
Lesson 1's 因為……而…… gives cause and result. 為了……而…… gives a goal and the action for it.
B3L11-G01-P289: 透過 means through or by way of. It names the person, channel or method that gets you a result.
Put the channel after 透過, before the verb: 有個博士透過社群網站，認識了一個女網友.
Don't mix it up with Lesson 2's 經過, which is passing through a place or process, not a channel.
B3L11-G02-P291: 以上 means at or above a number, and it includes that number. 八十分以上 (80 points and above) includes 80.
以下 means at or below a number, and it includes that number too: 兩萬塊以下 (20,000 dollars or less).
Both go after the number and measure word, as in 一千元以上, never before it.
以 with other place words marks a range in the same way, as in 以內 (within) and 以外 (outside).
B3L11-G03-P292: 看得起 means you respect someone and think they matter. 看不起 means you look down on them.
Put the person right after it: 主管看得起你, 你不可以看不起窮人.
Negate it inside the verb as 看不起, never with 不 in front.
Book 2 Lesson 4's V得起/V不起 is about affording something. 看得起 and 看不起 are about respect.
B3L11-G04-P299: 卻 means yet or but. The second part goes against the facts or against what you expected.
Put 卻 after the subject and before the verb: 我們卻聊不到幾句話 (yet we could hardly talk).
可是 can start the second part, but 卻 stays after the subject: 可是面對面接觸時，我們卻聊不到幾句話.
B3L11-G05-P301: 對得起 means you did right by someone, so you have nothing to feel bad about. 對不起 here means you let them down.
Put the person or group right after it: 怎麼對得起父母呢 (how could he face his parents), 對不起社會 (letting society down).
This 對不起 is a verb with someone after it. It is not the same as saying 對不起 alone to mean sorry.
B3L11-G06-P302: 至於 means as for. After you make one point, it turns to a related point.
Put the new point right after 至於, then comment on it: 至於詳細內容就得問他本人了 (as for the details, you'll have to ask him).
The point after 至於 is often an open question: 至於什麼時候舉行婚禮，還要問家長的意見.
Don't open a conversation with 至於. Say the first point, then use 至於 to move to the next.
B3L12-G01-P313: 這就 says you will do it right now. 這 means now and 就 means at once.
Put 這就 after the subject and before the action: 我這就通知經理 (I'll tell the manager right away).
It is only for right now, so never put a later time with it: no 明天這就.
B3L12-G02-P314: 在……方面 names the area you are talking about, and the rest of the sentence says what is true in it.
Put the area between 在 and 方面, and keep both words.
It can open the sentence (在穿著方面，白小姐很有品味) or follow the subject (你在這方面有經驗嗎).
對……來說 gives someone's point of view, not an area. Don't say 對穿著方面.
B3L12-G03-P316: 往往 says something usually happens under certain conditions. It describes a pattern seen again and again.
Put it before the verb, after the condition or topic: 透過良好的溝通，往往能解決不必要的麻煩 (good communication usually solves needless trouble).
Use it for general facts and what has happened so far, not for plans or wishes. 常常 is fine there.
Always say both characters, and never put 不 before it: no 不往往.
B3L12-G04-P318: 有關 means about or concerning. It usually starts the sentence to bring up a topic.
Put the topic right after it, then explain or advise: 有關這方面的問題，會有相關人員來跟你詳細說明.
Lesson 11's 'as for' turns to a second point. 有關 can bring up the main topic first.
B3L12-G05-P325: 儘管 means even though, like 雖然. It starts the first part and states something that is really true.
The second part gives the unexpected result, often with 但是, 可是, 還是 or 卻: 儘管已經下課了，張老師還是留在教室裡改作業.
Lesson 1's 'even if' (and 即使) is for something imagined. 儘管 is for a real fact.
B3L12-G06-P327: 不論……都…… says the result stays the same however the situation changes.
Follow 不論 with a question word, a choice with 或, opposites like 大小, or A-not-A like 去不去.
都 goes in the second part, after its subject: 不論你說什麼，他都不會改變 (whatever you say, he won't change). Don't leave it out.
It works like Book 2 Lesson 13's 'no matter', but sounds a bit more formal.
B3L13-G01-P338: 這下子 means now, after what just happened. Use it to react to news or a sudden change.
Put it at the start of your reaction, before the subject: 這下子他得改變計畫了 (now he'll have to change his plans).
現在 only tells the time. 這下子 points to the result of what just happened.
B3L13-G02-P339: 既……又…… means both … and … for one subject's two qualities or actions: 既省時間又方便.
Put 既 and 又 after the subject, before verbs or adjectives: 既要品質好，又要設計佳.
Both parts are good, or both are bad. Don't put 很 or 'very' in front of them.
The part after 又 weighs a little more. 既……又…… sounds more written than 又……又…….
B3L13-G03-P341: 更別說……了 means let alone or not to mention: the second case follows clearly from the first.
In a negative sentence, put the easy case with 連……都 first, then 更別說: 我奶奶連怎麼上傳資料都不會，更別說建立自己的網站了.
In a positive sentence, give the bigger point first, then 更別說: 既省時間又方便，更別說提供……基本服務了.
更別說 starts the second part, and 了 ends it.
B3L13-G04-P347: 就是……也…… means even if. Even if the situation after 就是 happens, the result after 也 stays the same.
Put 就是 before the imagined situation and 也 before the verb of the result: 人們就是不出門，也可透過網路滿足相關的需求.
If the result has its own subject, 也 goes after it: 就是吃再多苦，我也要堅持到底.
It works like Lesson 1's 就算……也……. Here 就是 never means exactly, and pairs with 也, not 就.
B3L13-G05-P348: 一方面……，一方面…… means on the one hand … on the other, giving two reasons, results or purposes.
With one subject, put it after the subject: 一方面要照顧生意，一方面要訓練員工, or add 也: 一方面也帶給企業更良好的管理方式.
If each part has its own subject, 一方面 goes before it: 一方面打了折之後便宜得多，一方面筆電該有的功能它都有.
The two parts weigh the same. With 不但……而且……, the second part goes a step further.
B3L14-G01-P360: 這就要從……說起了 says a topic is big, so you must start at one point: 這就要從你的飲食習慣說起了.
Put the starting point between 從 and the verb, and end with 起了, not 起來.
Other one-syllable verbs work too (看, 做, 寫, 找, 聊): 就要從兩年前的找起了. Two-syllable 說明 does not.
If the sentence before already named the topic, leave out 這 or 那.
B3L14-G02-P362: V下去 means to keep on doing something: 你們能堅持下去嗎 (can you keep it up)?
Nothing goes after 下去. Name the thing first as the topic: 這部電影很無聊，我實在看不下去了.
Put 得 or 不 between the verb and 下去 to say you can or can't keep going: 看不下去.
Book 2 Lesson 15's 'down/stay' complement is about keeping or resting, not going on.
B3L14-G03-P363: 幸虧 means luckily. It gives the lucky fact that stopped something bad, and 要不然 says what would have happened without it.
幸虧 starts the lucky part, before its subject: 幸虧她那天沒去，要不然就糟了.
It works like Book 2 Lesson 5's everyday 'luckily … otherwise …', in a slightly more formal tone.
B3L14-G04-P369: 根據 means according to. It names the source or evidence a statement or decision rests on.
Put 根據 and the source (說法, 法律, 調查, 報告) at the start: 根據我國的法律，十八歲以上才可以喝酒.
根據 tells why you can say something. 按照 tells how something is done.
B3L14-G05-P371: 按照 means following a rule, method, plan or standard. It is about how something is done.
Put 按照 and the rule before the verb: 只要按照醫生的話去做 (just do what the doctor says).
You can shorten it to 按 or 照: 就按會議的決定做吧 (let's do as the meeting decided).
Use 根據 to give the basis for a statement. 根據 can also be a noun, meaning basis. 按照 can't.
B3L15-G01-P383: 簡直 means practically or simply. The speaker exaggerates on purpose to paint a vivid picture.
Put it after the subject, before the verb or description: 那幾條龍簡直快飛起來了 (those dragons look practically ready to fly off).
It often comes before 像, 就像, 是 or 就是: 簡直像個仙女一樣 (just like a fairy).
很 and 非常 only say how much. 簡直 shows the speaker's own strong reaction.
B3L15-G02-P384: Vs得沒話說 says something is so good there are no better words for it.
Put the describing word right before 得沒話說: 夕陽美得沒話說, 速度快得沒話說.
It is only for praise. Book 2's 'extremely' patterns can describe bad feelings too.
沒話說 on its own can praise something too, as in 服務沒話說.
B3L15-G03-P392: 同時 has two uses: two things happen at the same time, or a second, equal point is added.
For the same time, put it after the subject and before the verb: 我們同時完成了 (we finished at the same time).
To add a point, start the second part with 同時, often with 也: 孔子是哲學方面的代表人物，同時也是華人最尊敬的老師.
一邊……一邊…… is one person doing two actions at once. 同時 also works for two people or two roles.
B3L15-G04-P393: 及 joins nouns and means the same as 和 or 跟, but it is more formal.
It is mostly for writing. Don't use it to join whole sentences.
With three or more items, put 及 only between the last two.
B3L15-G05-P395: 總而言之, or the shorter 總之, means in short. It sums up what was just said in one conclusion.
Put it at the start of the concluding sentence: 總而言之，大家應該要一起解決這個問題 (in short, everyone should work on this problem together).
總之 is the everyday form: 總之，各方面都得一百分才行.
Don't mix it up with 總算 from Lesson 6, which means finally, after a long wait.
B3L16-G01-P404: 當作, also written 當做, means to treat or take one thing as another, by mistake or on purpose.
Use 把 A 當作 B (把冰箱裡的水果酒當作果汁喝了) or 被當作 B (被當作垃圾丟掉).
With a whole clause after it, 當作 means acting as if it were true: 老師就當作你們都懂了.
Lesson 5's 'mistakenly thought' is only for wrong beliefs. 當作 also covers treating something so on purpose.
B3L16-G02-P406: 至少 means at least. It sets the lowest amount, level or step.
Put 至少 before the number or verb, never at the end: 至少兩個月才能完全恢復.
It often names the smallest step someone should take: 至少得先聽聽其他人的意見 (you should at least hear what others think first).
It can also point out one good thing in a bad situation: 至少不必擔心食物不夠.
B3L16-G03-P413: 由於 gives the cause, and 因此 gives the result. It means the same as 因為……，所以……, but sounds more formal.
由於 starts the first part. 因此 before the result can be left out: 由於這個都市規劃得不理想，商業活動增加後，交通就變得又擠又亂.
因為 can start either part, but if the cause comes second, write 是由於, not just 由於.
B3L16-G04-P415: 使得 means to cause or bring about: cause first, then 使得, then who or what is affected and the result.
九二一大地震的規模很大，使得許多房屋跟馬路都塌了 (the 921 earthquake was so strong that many houses and roads collapsed).
It is more formal than 使. Use 使得 for things that have happened, and 使 for imagined ones.
Unlike Lesson 10's bad-result verb, 使得 works for good results too: 使得參觀的民眾一年比一年多了.
B3L16-G05-P417: 於是 means so, as a result. It joins a situation to the action someone then takes because of it.
Put it at the start of the second part: 於是，他在餐廳門外放了一台冰箱.
Never use it for natural events or things nobody chose: no 天很黑，於是下雨了. Use 所以 there.
Lesson 5's 'as a result' tells how things turned out. 於是 tells what someone chose to do next.
